title: How to Manage Department-Wise Expense Limits in Frappe?

posts.cooked:
We want to set monthly or quarterly expense limits for each department (e.g., Marketing, Sales, IT) and track employee spending against those limits.

Ideally, the system should:

  • Tag Expense Claims to the correct department
  • Alert department heads when spending is near the limit
  • Stop or escalate claims that go over budget

We’re using Cost Centers and Budgets, but it’s not clear how to enforce these controls automatically.

posts.name: Ahsan Tareen
posts.cooked:
Hi @JitenDhabhi1354

You can make Department doctype as Accounting Dimension and then set Budget against each Department and the Budgeted Amount can be distributed as per your requirements on Monthly basis by defining Monthly Distribution within Budget docytpe as well.

Knowing the fact Budgets are defined against GL Accounts within a Fiscal Year and in your particular use case , the Recording Phase takes effect provided GL Accounts, Department and fiscal year matches. The Most of the recording elements are itemized where you have to pick and choose items (stock items, service items and Assets) in different docytpes child tables and you have to make sure correct GL Account with rest of the dimension are linked so that budget can play its part.

Due to Itemized nature of the ERP, Item Manager (Role) has to be someone within house as a super user to control accounting elements based on items so that any other user on Basic Recording phase should not change those settings and each expense record should go under respective department budget with its defaults. The Role Permission Manager and User Permissions are where you should control Basic Recording levels and make sure each user should follow correct expense recordings.

The Notification Module will help triggering notification on any event during recording phases of expense under budgets. The Auto email report can help manager to be notified existing or remaining limit on their budget periodically.

This is how Budget takes effect and play its part effectively.
